blurb: One root, two great journeys: through Germanic it became bear, birth and burden; through Latin and Greek it became fertile, transfer, offer and metaphor.
The PIE word for water flowed into water and wet, Russian vodka, Greek hydro- and Latin unda (wave), giving redundant and abundance.
Know, can and cunning on the Germanic side; noble, ignore, notice and diagnosis via Latin and Greek.
Foot and fetter; Latin pes gave pedal, pedestrian and impede; Greek pous gave octopus and podium.
The moon measured time: moon, month, measure, meter, dimension.

meaning: to set, to put, to do
blurb: Do and deed in Germanic; Latin facere (fact, factory, affect, perfect) and Greek thesis and theme.
Star, astronomy, asterisk, stellar and disaster — literally a bad star.
Kin, kind and king; gene, genius, nature, nation, native and pregnant.
Light, lunar, lucid, illuminate, lux and lynx (the bright-eyed cat).
-ward, worth and weird; Latin vertere gave verse, version, convert, prose and vertebra.
The shining sky-god: Tuesday, Zeus, Jupiter, divine, deity, diary and journal.
Wit, wise and wisdom; vision, video, evidence; Greek idea and history; Celtic druid.
Heart; Latin cor gave cordial, courage and record; Greek kardia gave cardiac.
Mother, maternal, matrix, matter and metropolis.
Father; Latin pater gave paternal, patron, pattern and patriot.
Two, twin, twelve, between; dual, double, dozen, diploma.
New, novel, novice, renovate, neon.
Night, nocturnal, equinox.
Hound in Germanic; canine, kennel and canary via Latin; cynic via Greek (the dog-like philosophers).
Old English eoh died out, but the root lives on in equine, equestrian and hippopotamus (river horse).
A stranger could be a guest or an enemy: guest, host, hostile, hospital, hotel, hostage.
Salt; salary, salad, sauce, sausage, salsa, saline.
Horn, hart; unicorn and cornea; Greek keras gave rhinoceros and carrot.
Stand, stead, stool; state, station, stable, obstacle; Greek system and ecstasy.

blurb: Right and rich; regal, reign, rule, direct, realm; Sanskrit raja.
Cow in Germanic; beef via French; bovine via Latin; butter and bucolic via Greek.
Tooth; dental, dentist, dandelion (lion's tooth); orthodontist.
Eke and nickname; auction, augment, author and August.
Murder; mortal, mortgage (a death-pledge) and ambrosia (food of the immortals).
Spy; spectacle, inspect, despise; Greek skopos gave telescope, sceptic and bishop.
Flow, flood, fly, flee; pluvial; Greek pneumonia.
Gather words and you speak them: lecture, legend, logic, lexicon, catalogue and every -logy.
Human, humble, humus; Greek chameleon (ground lion); and the groom in bridegroom.
Sister; sorority; cousin.
Name; noun, nominate, renown; Greek onoma gave anonymous and synonym.
Wolf; Greek lykos gave lycanthrope; Latin lupus gave lupine.
Yellow, gold, gleam, glass, glow; Greek chlorine (pale green).
Break, breach; fraction, fragile, fracture.
Three, thrice, third; trio, trinity, tripod.
Hundred; cent, century, percent; Greek hekaton; Sanskrit śata.
Mind; mental, mention, monitor; Greek mania, mentor; Sanskrit mantra.
Act, agent, agile; Greek agony, protagonist; acre.
Hell, hall, helmet, hole; cell, conceal, color; Greek apocalypse.
Way, weigh, wagon, wiggle; vehicle, vector, convey, vex.
Give, gift; habit, able, exhibit, prohibit.
Bite, bitter, boat; fissure.
Second, sequence, sect, consequence, pursue, suit.
Worse, war (via Frankish werra), guerrilla.
